title: Confidence Inversion in Open-Set Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition: A Leakage-Safe Multi-Corpus Pilot
content: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) systems are usually evaluated in closed label spaces, although deployment exposes them to unseen targets and shifted acquisition conditions. We evaluate five score/loss configurations—a ResNet-18 classifier trained with cross-entropy (CE) or the entropic open-set loss (EOS), scored by maximum softmax probability (MSP), the energy score, or OpenMax—across six recording-disjoint protocols spanning four corpora (3 seeds each): four intra-corpus class holdouts and two cross-corpus domain-shifted unknown settings in opposite directions. CE+MSP falls below chance-level AUROC on the Oceanship holdout and the QiandaoEar22→Oceanship cross-corpus protocol (0.34–0.37): unknown samples can receive higher confidence than known samples under acquisition shift. Energy scoring improves AUROC in these inverted protocols (+0.21 and +0.12 across the three evaluated seeds; nominal paired-test p ≤ 0.013), training-free, whereas OpenMax and EOS show protocol-dependent gains and regressions; even the best logit-space result retains a 0.87 unknown false-acceptance rate at 95% known acceptance. Post-hoc feature-space scoring on the same frozen encoders gives a different pattern: a ViM-style residual score reaches 0.934 and 0.939 AUROC on the two cross-corpus protocols (FPR@95TPR 0.205 and 0.405), but only 0.640 on the Oceanship intra-corpus holdout—separability that conventional logit-space confidence does not capture. This separability may reflect acquisition-domain differences rather than semantic vessel novelty: feature-space residual scoring substantially improves detection of the compound cross-corpus unknowns evaluated here, whereas within-corpus novel-class rejection remains unresolved.
